types.name: Configuration and properties
types.desc: Pool configuration nvlists (from labels, the cachefile, tryimport or the MOS), vdev trees, uberblocks read from the labels, load information returned to userspace, property lists.

types.name: Block pointer
types.desc: The root block pointer of the MOS, taken from the selected uberblock.

types.name: I/O request
types.desc: Block reads through the zio pipeline (MOS reads, verification reads).

types.name: Intent-log record
types.desc: Log chains and log blocks read, claimed or replayed.

types.name: Transaction
types.desc: Starting, waiting for and stopping txg syncs.

types.name: Device I/O
types.desc: Label, uberblock and probe I/O at fixed offsets on a leaf device.

types.name: Control
types.desc: Calls that carry no configuration or payload: requests, checks, verdicts, errors. Draw dashed.

contexts.name: Userspace (`zpool` command, libzfs, libzutil, systemd units)
Kernel, in the thread of the calling process (an ioctl on /dev/zfs, mount(2) or umount(2)) or a helper thread it starts, outside syncing context and outside any dmu_tx
Open context: the calling thread (syscall / zvol worker), inside a dmu_tx
Syncing context: txg_sync thread or dp_sync_taskq workers, one txg at a time
A dedicated kernel thread or zthr
Runs in whichever context calls it

groups.title: Userspace - zpool, libzfs, libzutil

nodes.title: Administrator
nodes.role: The person or script typing the command. Every path in this graph that a command starts begins with a wire from this node; the arrows that come back into a command node are its results, errors and refusals.

nodes.title: Boot import services (systemd)
nodes.role: At boot on Linux with systemd, `zfs-import-cache.service` runs `zpool import -c /etc/zfs/zpool.cache -aN`; when the cachefile is missing or empty, `zfs-import-scan.service` runs `zpool import -aN -o cachefile=none` instead. Both import without mounting (`-N`); `zfs-mount.service` later runs `zfs mount -a`. The kernel module itself imports nothing at load time: the cachefile is read only by userspace.

nodes.title: zpool(8) command
nodes.role: `zpool import` builds the search arguments (`-d` directories or `ZPOOL_IMPORT_PATH`, `-c` cachefile, `-s` scan, pool name or numeric guid) and the load policy (`-F` do rewind, `-n` try rewind, `-X` extreme rewind, `-T` txg, `-M` relaxed metadata checks), searches, then lists the pools (no argument), imports all (`-a`, in parallel on a taskq) or the one named. `-o name=value` sets a pool property, `-o opts` gives mount options, `-R` sets altroot and cachefile=none. A failed `-c` import is retried once by scanning the directories named in the cachefile. `zpool export` unmounts and exports each named pool, or all pools in parallel with `-a`.

nodes.title: Host check (zfs_force_import_required)
nodes.role: The only place the classic `-f` check lives: a pool whose state is not EXPORTED and whose hostid (from the MOS config, via tryimport) differs from this system's needs `-f`. It also refuses, without `-f`, when tryimport saw MMP activity or the pool has multihost=on and this system has no hostid. The kernel never reads the `-f` flag (ZFS_IMPORT_ANY_HOST).

nodes.title: libzfs mount / unmount
nodes.role: After an import, `zpool_enable_datasets()` gathers every file system of the pool, mounts them in mountpoint order with a pool of threads (datasets whose key is not loaded are skipped), then shares them one by one. Before an export, `zpool_disable_datasets()` takes the pool's file systems from the mount table, not from the pool, unshares them, then unmounts them in reverse mountpoint order; `-f` passes MS_FORCE. Volumes are not handled here.

nodes.title: Pool search (zpool_search_import)
nodes.role: Chooses between the cachefile and a device search. For a device search it opens every candidate on a taskq (about two threads per CPU), reads its labels, keeps those of the requested pool (by name or guid, spares and cache devices always), drops devices that cannot be opened exclusively (for example multipath members), and hands the labels to configuration assembly.

nodes.title: Device discovery (blkid / directory scan)
nodes.role: Produces the list of candidate devices. By default on Linux it asks libblkid for every device of TYPE zfs_member. With `-d`, ZPOOL_IMPORT_PATH or `-s` it lists every entry of the given directories, or of the default search path (/dev/disk/by-vdev, /dev/mapper, by-partlabel, by-partuuid, by-label, by-uuid, by-id, by-path, then /dev). Each candidate gets a preference order, used later to pick the best name for a device found under several paths.

nodes.title: Cachefile reader
nodes.role: `zpool import -c <file>`: reads and unpacks the whole cachefile and takes each pool's configuration from it as is, skipping pools already imported. No label is read in userspace, so paths in the cachefile must still be right. In the fallback scan after a failed cachefile import, only the directories that hold the cached device paths are scanned for that pool's guid.

nodes.title: Label reader (zpool_open_func)
nodes.role: Opens one candidate read-only (O_DIRECT when possible, to avoid stale multipath caches) and reads the configuration nvlist of each of its four labels in one asynchronous batch. The first valid label supplies the config and the others with the same vdev guid are counted; labels with txg 0 (written before the device was in use) are skipped, and a device with no valid label is ignored. When a label names another path or devid for the same vdev, that path is tried too. Uberblocks are not read in userspace.

nodes.title: Configuration assembly (get_configs)
nodes.role: Groups the labels by pool guid, then by top-level vdev guid, then by txg. For each top-level vdev the label with the highest txg supplies that vdev's subtree; the pool-wide fields (name, state, hostid, number of top-level vdevs, holes) come from the newest label of all. Missing top-level vdevs become placeholders. Each device's path is set to the best name it was found under. Pools already imported here are dropped, and each remaining configuration is sent to the kernel for a tryimport.

nodes.title: libzfs import / tryimport
nodes.role: Wraps the two import ioctls. `refresh_config()` sends a configuration for a tryimport and returns the kernel's version of it. `zpool_import_props()` validates the new name and the `-o` properties, sends the import, and turns the kernel's errors and load information into messages: unsupported features, the host that holds the pool, missing log devices, or what a rewind would cost.

nodes.title: libzfs export
nodes.role: Sends ZFS_IOC_POOL_EXPORT. `zpool_export()` passes force (from `zpool export -f`), which only overrides the active shared spare check; `zpool_export_force()` (from `-F`) also passes hardforce. The caller must have unmounted the file systems first.

nodes.title: Pool ioctls (tryimport, import, export)
nodes.role: Kernel entry for ZFS_IOC_POOL_TRYIMPORT, ZFS_IOC_POOL_IMPORT and ZFS_IOC_POOL_EXPORT. Import and tryimport return the configuration, including the load information, in the destination nvlist even when they fail, which is how userspace learns why.

nodes.title: spa_tryimport()
nodes.role: Loads the pool read-only under a temporary name (`$import-<thread>-<pool>`) with a missing log device tolerated, then generates a full configuration from whatever opened: vdev tree with states, pool state, the loaded uberblock's timestamp, the load information (MMP state, enabled and unsupported features, the MOS hostid and hostname), spares, cache devices and bootfs. Then it unloads and removes the temporary pool. Nothing is written.

nodes.title: spa_import()
nodes.role: Refuses a name already in use, creates the spa_t, activates it read-write or read-only (`readonly=on` in the properties), keeps async work suspended, loads the pool with the rewind policy, and on success applies the properties, refreshes spares and cache devices, updates the config and cachefile (writeable pools only), requests autoexpand, logs the import in the pool history and creates zvol devices. On failure it unloads and removes the spa_t again.

nodes.title: spa_export_common()
nodes.role: Export (and, with other states, destroy and reset). Marks the pool as exporting, stops async work, waits for a txg so that objsets held only by dirty data are released, then refuses with EBUSY if anything still holds the pool. Removes zvol devices, refuses an active shared spare unless forced, stops initialize, TRIM, rebuild and L2ARC rebuild, sets the pool state to EXPORTED and dirties every label (unless hardforce), may flush metaslabs to shrink the log space maps, fixes the final txg, unloads, rewrites the cachefile without the pool (unless hardforce) and removes it from the namespace.

nodes.title: spa_unload()
nodes.role: Tears a loaded pool down: stops the sync threads after the final txgs, stops the MMP thread, waits for outstanding async I/O, closes every vdev, closes the DSL pool and unloads DDT, BRT and the log space maps. Also used between load attempts and after a tryimport.

nodes.title: SPA namespace
nodes.role: The kernel's AVL tree of spa_t by name, under spa_namespace_lock. A pool is "imported" exactly while it is in this tree. `spa_add()` also decides the cachefile: the default path unless an altroot is given. A lookup of a pool that is being exported waits until the export finishes.

nodes.title: spa_load_best(): rewind loop
nodes.role: Runs `spa_load()` and, when it fails for a reason a rewind could fix, loads again with the maximum txg set just below the uberblock that failed, until a load succeeds or the minimum txg is passed: the newest txg minus TXG_DEFER_SIZE normally, TXG_INITIAL with `-X`. In RECOVER state (`-F`) the first good load is the pool and the intent logs are discarded. Otherwise the original error is returned and the older loads, which wrote nothing, are reported as rewind information. Errors that a rewind cannot fix (another host active, interrupted, no checkpoint) end the search at once.

nodes.title: spa_load() / spa_load_impl()
nodes.role: Drives the load phases in order: parse the provided config, open and validate the vdevs, select the uberblock, open the MOS, switch to the trusted config, optional checkpoint rewind, checkpoint txg, indirect vdevs, features, special directories, properties, spares and cache devices, vdev metadata, dedup tables, BRT, log checks, verification. Only for a writeable load at the newest txg (or in RECOVER state) does it go on to claim the logs, start the sync and MMP threads, wait for the claims to sync, request a config update and a resilver if needed, restart removals, clean up inconsistent datasets and restart initialize and TRIM. Posts an ereport when the load fails.

nodes.title: Parse the provided config
nodes.role: Turns the configuration from userspace into an in-memory vdev tree. This config is untrusted: until the MOS copy is loaded the pool cannot be written. Refuses a pool guid that is already imported (EEXIST).

nodes.title: vdev_open() / vdev_reopen()
nodes.role: Opens the whole tree bottom-up; each leaf is opened through its driver and probed with a test read. A mirror or raidz with enough children left is DEGRADED, otherwise it cannot open. The root opens only if no more top-level vdevs are missing than allowed: zfs_max_missing_tvds_cachefile (2) for an untrusted config from a cachefile, zfs_max_missing_tvds_scan (0) from a scan, never fewer than zfs_max_missing_tvds; a pool with a top-level vdev missing can be opened only read-only.

nodes.title: vdev_validate(): labels vs config
nodes.role: Reads each readable leaf's label (the two at the start of the device first, because the trailing pair moves when a device grows) and checks it against the config: the vdev guid and top-level guid must match, the pool guid too once the config is trusted, and a vdev split off into another pool is refused. A leaf that fails is marked CANT_OPEN; the load fails if that leaves the root unopenable.

nodes.title: Uberblock selection
nodes.role: Reads every uberblock slot of every trusted label of every readable leaf and keeps the best one not above spa_load_max_txg: highest txg, then latest timestamp, then highest MMP sequence. Each sync writes its uberblock into slot txg modulo the ring size, so the rings hold the most recent txgs. The configuration of that uberblock's txg is then read from the same leaf. Runs the multihost check, refuses an unsupported version or an unknown feature in the label's features_for_read, and sets the first txg the pool will write: normally the loaded txg + 1, but above the newest uberblock seen when an older txg was requested.

nodes.title: MMP activity check and claim
nodes.role: For a pool whose uberblock shows MMP in use, unless it was exported by this very host (or destroyed). A system without a hostid is refused. At tryimport the best uberblock is reread about once a second for the check duration: by default the owner's fail intervals times its MMP interval times 2 (20 s with the defaults), plus up to 25% at random; any change means another host is active. At import the tryimport result is reused when the uberblock is unchanged; then, once the trusted config is loaded, the host claims the pool: ten times, one MMP interval apart, it writes the best uberblock with a random sequence to an MMP slot of every writeable leaf and reads back that its own write is the best. The `-f` flag does not skip any of this. A rewind (`-F`, state RECOVER) skips the watch; the claim is skipped only for an extreme rewind.

nodes.title: Open the MOS (dsl_pool_init)
nodes.role: Creates the DSL pool at the first txg and opens the MOS objset from the uberblock's root block pointer. From here on every phase reads MOS objects through the normal read path.

nodes.title: Trusted config from the MOS
nodes.role: Loads the pool configuration stored in the MOS, builds a new vdev tree from it, copies the device paths over from the provided config (which came from the scan or the cachefile, so its paths are current), replaces the old tree and marks the config trusted, which makes the pool writeable. Reopens and revalidates the vdevs. If the provided config missed top-level vdevs that the MOS knows, the whole MOS init is redone once with the trusted config, so a newer uberblock on those vdevs is not missed. Then the multihost claim, the missing log check and the check that the vdev guid sum matches the uberblock's. Records the MOS hostid and hostname in the load information.

nodes.title: Checkpoint rewind
nodes.role: `zpool import --rewind-to-checkpoint`: reads the checkpointed uberblock saved in the MOS, gives it the current txg + 1 and the current time so it outranks every uberblock on disk, and on a writeable import writes it to the labels. The load then starts over from that uberblock. Imported read-only, the checkpointed state can be inspected without writing anything.

nodes.title: Feature flags check
nodes.role: Compares the features the MOS lists as needed for reading, and for writing when the import is writeable or a tryimport, with the features this software knows. An unknown read feature refuses the pool; an unknown write feature refuses a writeable import but allows `-o readonly=on`, which userspace is told through ZPOOL_CONFIG_CAN_RDONLY. Loads every feature's reference count into memory.

nodes.title: MOS metadata load
nodes.role: Opens the DSL directories, reads the pool properties (and forces failmode=continue when top-level vdevs are missing), opens spares and cache devices, loads each vdev's metaslab array, space maps and DTLs, then the dedup tables and the block reference table. With autoreplace=on, unopenable devices are reported for replacement.

nodes.title: Log device checks
nodes.role: A log device that cannot be opened refuses the import with ENXIO and is listed for the user, unless `-m` (ZFS_IMPORT_MISSING_LOG), which drops the intent log instead (tryimport always behaves as if `-m` was given). On a writeable import every dataset's log chain is also checked; a broken chain refuses the import unless top-level vdevs are missing.

nodes.title: spa_load_verify(): recent txgs
nodes.role: Not for a tryimport. Traverses every block born after spa_verify_min_txg (the last few txgs; the whole pool with `-X`) and reads metadata blocks, and data blocks only when the count is reported (`zpool import -nF`), at scrub priority with at most 1/2^spa_load_verify_shift of the ARC target in flight. By default any metadata error fails the load with EIO, which is what makes a rewind try an older txg; `-M` counts errors in non-critical metadata as data errors. On success the txg, its timestamp and the error counts go into the load information.

nodes.title: zpl mount (zfs_domount)
nodes.role: mount(2) of a ZFS file system: owns the dataset, sets up the zfsvfs, opens its ZIL and, on a writeable pool, replays it before the mount completes (a read-only mount lifts its read-only flag for the replay). Linux names; FreeBSD has the equivalents in its own zfs_vfsops.c.

nodes.title: Kernel unmount (zfs_umount)
nodes.role: umount(2) of a ZFS file system: `zfsvfs_teardown()` closes the ZIL, so outstanding log records are committed, and the dataset is disowned, which drops its hold on the pool. Until every file system of the pool is unmounted this way, the export cannot pass its reference check.

nodes.title: zil_claim() / zil_replay()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. At import, `zil_claim()` runs for every dataset in one tx of the first txg: it walks the log chain and marks each log block born after the last synced txg as allocated, so the allocator cannot hand it out before replay, and records that a replay is needed. When the log is being cleared (rewind, `-m`, a checkpoint rewind) the chain is freed instead. At mount, `zil_replay()` re-executes each claimed record as a normal transaction and then destroys the log.

nodes.title: TXG: syncing (txg_sync_thread)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Started by a writeable import once the logs are claimed; never started for a read-only import. At export, `txg_sync_stop()` waits for the open txg plus TXG_DEFER_SIZE to sync, then stops the quiesce and sync threads.

nodes.title: spa_sync()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Each txg ends with the label and uberblock update, and then dispatches pending async requests.

nodes.title: Uberblock + label update

ref.code: vdev_config_sync(spa_t *spa, vdev_t **svd, int svdcount, uint64_t txg,
uberblock_update(uberblock_t *ub, vdev_t *rvd, uint64_t txg, uint64_t mmp_delay)

nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. When the configuration is dirty (after an import, at export) every label of every vdev is rewritten with the current config, which carries the pool state, this host's hostid and hostname; otherwise only uberblocks are written, to a few top-level vdevs. Also writes the checkpointed uberblock during a checkpoint rewind.

nodes.title: Label / uberblock writer

ref.code: vdev_label_sync_list(spa_t *spa, int l, uint64_t txg, int flags)
vdev_label_write(zio_t *zio, vdev_t *vd, int l, abd_t *buf, uint64_t offset,

nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Writes the even labels, then the uberblock, then the odd labels, flushing the disk write caches after each step, so that a crash at any point leaves labels that match a valid uberblock.

nodes.title: MMP heartbeat thread
nodes.role: Started with every writeable import, writes only while multihost=on. It keeps rewriting the last synced uberblock, with a fresh timestamp and sequence number, into the reserved MMP slots of the label rings: one leaf every zfs_multihost_interval divided by the number of leaves. This is the heartbeat another host's import watches for. If no write succeeds for zfs_multihost_fail_intervals times the interval it suspends the pool, so it stops writing before an importer's check could end.

nodes.title: spa_async_thread()
nodes.role: Work requested during import that runs once the pool is up: the config and cachefile update, the resilver, autoexpand events (only with autoexpand=on), L2ARC rebuild and the sweep of deferred snapshot destroys. Requests are only recorded; the thread is started at the end of a spa_sync() and not while async work is suspended (during the import itself and from the start of an export).

nodes.title: Resilver trigger
nodes.role: At the end of a writeable import, a sequential rebuild that was in progress is resumed; otherwise, if no resilver is already running and any leaf's DTL records txgs it missed, a resilver is requested from the async thread.

nodes.title: Pool suspend / resume
nodes.role: Reached here from the MMP thread when heartbeat writes stop landing: the pool suspends with ZIO_SUSPEND_MMP. `zpool clear` resumes it only after checking that no other host has imported the pool meanwhile.

nodes.title: Pool cache file (zpool.cache)

ref.code: spa_config_generate(spa_t *spa, vdev_t *vd, uint64_t txg, int getstats)

nodes.role: The kernel code that keeps the cachefile up to date, run in the ioctl thread for import and export and in the async thread for later updates. `spa_config_update()` dirties every label and waits for that txg, so the labels carry the new config, then writes the cachefile. `spa_write_cachefile()` writes, for each cachefile this pool uses or used, the configs of every writeable pool that uses it, in place (truncate, write, fsync); a cachefile left with no pools is removed. Read-only pools and pools with cachefile=none (or an altroot) are never written.

nodes.title: Leaf vdev driver
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Opens a leaf device by the absolute path in the config (Linux `vdev_disk_open()`, which retries for a short while when the device node does not exist yet; FreeBSD `vdev_geom_open()`), and releases it when the vdev is closed.

nodes.title: Labels L0-L3 + uberblock ring
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Four labels per leaf, two at the start and two at the end of the device. Each holds the vdev configuration nvlist (pool name and guid, state, txg, hostid and hostname, this vdev's top-level subtree) and a ring of uberblocks; with multihost=on the last slots of each ring are reserved for MMP writes.

nodes.title: Data disks (normal class)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Here: where the MOS and the blocks checked by `spa_load_verify()` are read from.

nodes.title: SLOG (log class)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Holds the intent-log chains that are claimed at import and replayed at mount; without a log device the chains are in the main pool.

nodes.title: zpool.cache file on disk
nodes.role: /etc/zfs/zpool.cache unless the cachefile property names another file: one packed nvlist with the configuration of every pool that uses it. Written only by the kernel, read only by userspace (`zpool import -c`, the boot service). It saves the device scan at boot. A stale one cannot make the kernel load the wrong state, because the kernel checks it against the labels and the MOS; at worst the import fails and zpool(8) falls back to a scan.

wires.label: zpool import: zpool_do_import() gathers -d, -c, -s, the pool name or guid and the load policy, then zpool_search_import()
zpool_find_import(): candidates from libblkid (zpool_find_import_blkid()) by default, or zpool_find_import_scan() of the -d directories, ZPOOL_IMPORT_PATH or, with -s, the default search path
zpool_find_import_impl(): one zpool_open_func() task per candidate device on a taskq
zpool_read_label(): the configuration nvlist of all four labels in one lio_listio() batch, opened O_DIRECT when the device allows it; no uberblock is read
labels of the requested pool (of every pool when listing), from devices that open with O_EXCL, go to add_config(): grouped by pool guid, top-level vdev guid and txg
get_configs(): per top-level vdev the newest label config, merged into one pool config, paths fixed by fix_paths(), pools already imported skipped, then zutil_refresh_config()
refresh_config(): ZFS_IOC_POOL_TRYIMPORT with the assembled config
zfs_ioc_pool_tryimport() -> spa_tryimport()
spa_add() under a temporary name, spa_activate(SPA_MODE_READ); spa_remove() when done
spa_load(SPA_LOAD_TRYIMPORT), with ZFS_IMPORT_MISSING_LOG set so a missing log device does not stop the probe
spa_ld_mos_init() -> spa_ld_parse_config() -> spa_config_parse(): the provided config becomes an untrusted vdev tree; a pool guid already imported is EEXIST
spa_ld_open_vdevs() -> vdev_open() on the root vdev, with the number of missing top-level vdevs allowed for this config source
each leaf: vdev_op_open, Linux vdev_disk_open() or FreeBSD vdev_geom_open(), opens the device by its configured path
vdev_open() -> vdev_probe(): test reads of the pad area of labels 1 to 3 through the leaf before it counts as open; a failed probe faults the leaf
spa_ld_validate_vdevs() -> vdev_validate(), every leaf in parallel
vdev_label_read_config(): vdev guid and top-level guid must match the config, the pool guid too once it is trusted; otherwise the leaf is CANT_OPEN
spa_ld_select_uberblock(): find the uberblock to load

vdev_uberblock_load(): every uberblock slot of every trusted label of every readable leaf; the best not above spa_load_max_txg wins (txg, then timestamp, then MMP sequence); then the label config for its txg from the same leaf
spa_activity_check_required(): MMP in use in the uberblock and the pool not exported by this host: spa_ld_activity_check()
vdev_uberblock_load() again: about once a second during the tryimport check, after each claim write during import; a change in txg, timestamp or sequence means another host is writing
verdict, also stored in the load information: no hostid on this system, activity seen or claim failed (EREMOTEIO), interrupted (EINTR), or inactive
version and features_for_read supported: spa_ld_open_rootbp() -> dsl_pool_init() opens the MOS at the uberblock's root block pointer
no valid uberblock (ENXIO), or an unsupported version or features_for_read entry (ENOTSUP, listed in ZPOOL_CONFIG_UNSUP_FEAT): the load fails
dmu_objset_open_impl() reads the MOS objset block through the normal read path (arc_read()); every later phase reads MOS objects the same way
spa_ld_trusted_config(): load the config object from the MOS, rebuild the vdev tree from it with spa_config_parse(), copy the device paths from the provided config
config trusted: spa_ld_open_vdevs() and spa_ld_validate_vdevs() again on the new tree; missing top-level vdevs now refuse a writeable import
the provided config missed SPA_SYNC_MIN_VDEVS or more top-level vdevs the MOS knows: EAGAIN, spa_ld_prepare_for_reload(), and the MOS init runs again with the trusted config
import (not tryimport, not extreme rewind) of a pool that needed the activity check: spa_activity_check_claim()

mmp_claim_uberblock(): the best uberblock with a random MMP sequence to an MMP slot of every writeable leaf, then a cache flush; a leaf the config expects but that cannot be written fails the claim (ENODEV)
spa_check_for_missing_logs(): an unopenable log device is ENXIO unless -m, which sets SPA_LOG_CLEAR
--rewind-to-checkpoint: spa_ld_checkpoint_rewind() reads the checkpointed uberblock from the MOS directory and renumbers it above the current one
writeable import: vdev_config_sync(VDEV_CONFIG_REWINDING_CHECKPOINT) writes the checkpointed uberblock to the labels; from then on the rewind cannot be undone
spa_ld_prepare_for_reload(), then spa_ld_mos_with_trusted_config() again from the checkpointed uberblock
spa_ld_check_features(): features_for_read from the MOS, and features_for_write when writeable or a tryimport, checked by spa_features_check()
an unknown feature: ENOTSUP with the list in ZPOOL_CONFIG_UNSUP_FEAT, plus ZPOOL_CONFIG_CAN_RDONLY when only write features are unknown
special directories (dsl_pool_open()), pool properties, spares and cache devices, vdev metadata, dedup tables, BRT
spa_ld_verify_logs(): on a writeable import spa_check_logs() checks every dataset's log chain with zil_check_log_chain()
spa_ld_verify_pool_data() -> spa_load_verify(), skipped for a tryimport
traverse_pool() from spa_verify_min_txg: zio_read() at scrub priority of each metadata block (and data block when the count is reported) born after it

paths.summary: `zpool import` with no pool name. Userspace reads the labels of every candidate device and assembles one configuration per pool; the kernel test-loads each read-only and reports what it found. Nothing is written anywhere.

After the search and tryimport of path `discover`, zpool(8) checks the host, the kernel loads the pool for real, and a writeable load ends by claiming the logs, starting the sync thread and rewriting labels and cachefile. Then the file systems are mounted.

paths.summary: The heart of every import: the best uberblock on any readable device decides the txg the pool returns to, and its root block pointer opens the MOS. If the userspace config missed devices that the MOS knows about, the selection is repeated with the trusted config.

paths.title: multihost=on: the owner's heartbeat
paths.summary: What the importing host is watching for. While the pool is imported with `multihost=on`, the MMP thread writes a fresh copy of the last synced uberblock to some leaf several times per interval. If those writes stop landing, the owner suspends the pool before an importer's check can conclude that it is gone.
paths.ends: With writes landing, any importing host sees activity within its check. Without, the pool is suspended (`zfs-fault-management:suspend_clear`), and `zpool clear` resumes it only after verifying that no other host imported it in the meantime.

paths.summary: Some devices of the pool are absent. Redundancy decides: a missing mirror side or raidz child within parity leaves the pool DEGRADED but importable; a missing log device needs `-m`; a missing top-level vdev can only be imported read-only, after raising zfs_max_missing_tvds.

paths.title: zpool import -o readonly=on
paths.summary: A read-only import loads the pool exactly like a normal one but stops before every step that writes: no log claim, no sync thread, no MMP heartbeat, no label or cachefile update. It also accepts a pool whose unknown features are needed only for writing.
paths.ends: The pool is imported read-only. The labels still show the state and host of the last writeable import, the intent logs are untouched for a later read-write import, and an export writes nothing to the labels because no sync thread runs.

features_for_write are not checked
not writeable: the claim, sync start, config update and resilver steps of spa_load_impl() are skipped

paths.title: Intent logs: claimed at import, replayed at mount
paths.summary: Synchronous writes that reached the intent log but not a synced txg survive an unclean shutdown only in the log chains. Import claims their blocks so nothing overwrites them; each file system replays its own log when it is mounted.
paths.ends: The file system is mounted with every logged synchronous write applied; the log is empty. The replay of one write record is `zfs-io-flow:crash_replay`.

steps.note: claim: log blocks born after the last synced txg are claimed; zil_claim() marks the header ZIL_REPLAY_NEEDED
txg_wait_synced(spa_claim_max_txg): the claims are synced before the import returns
replay: the claimed chain is read again and each record re-executed

paths.title: Boot: import from the cachefile
paths.summary: At boot the import service imports every pool in /etc/zfs/zpool.cache without scanning devices and without mounting. If that import fails, zpool(8) retries once by scanning only the directories the cachefile's device paths are in.
paths.ends: The pools are imported but nothing is mounted (`-N`); `zfs-mount.service` mounts them later with `zfs mount -a`, which also replays their logs. Without a cachefile, `zfs-import-scan.service` imports by scanning (path `discover`, then `import` with `-aN`) and keeps the pools out of any cachefile.

paths.title: zpool export
paths.summary: Unmounts the pool's file systems, then the kernel checks that nothing holds the pool, lets the last txgs sync with every label marked EXPORTED, closes the devices and forgets the pool.
paths.ends: Normal and `-f`: the labels say EXPORTED, the pool is gone from the kernel and the cachefile, and any host can import it without `-f` (this host also skips the MMP check). `-F`: the pool is gone from the kernel, but labels and cachefile still describe an active pool, as after a crash. `busy`: the pool stays imported, already unmounted.

-f: force the unmounts and ignore an active shared spare
-F: hard force, no EXPORTED labels and no cachefile update
refused because the pool is still in use

nothing dirtied the labels: at most uberblocks are written and the labels still say ACTIVE

paths.title: zpool import --rewind-to-checkpoint
paths.summary: A pool with a checkpoint (`zpool checkpoint`) can be imported at the checkpointed state. The checkpointed uberblock saved in the MOS is renumbered to outrank everything on disk, written to the labels, and the load starts over from it.
paths.ends: `rw`: the pool is back at the checkpoint and everything written after it is gone for good. `ro`: the checkpointed state is imported read-only and the pool on disk is unchanged.

options.label: rewind for good
with -o readonly=on: inspect the checkpointed state, write nothing

steps.note: the checkpointed uberblock is now the best one on disk
read-only: the labels were not written, so the checkpointed uberblock in memory is used directly
log blocks from after the checkpoint may have been overwritten: unclaimed chains are cleared

paths.title: After import: resilver, config update, autoexpand
paths.summary: Work that the import only requests. Async work stays suspended for the whole load and is started by the end of a later spa_sync(), so the import returns before any of it runs.
paths.ends: The labels and the cachefile describe the pool as this host imported it, and a resilver of the devices that missed writes is under way (`zfs-scrub-resilver:resilver`).

steps.note: for example a disk that was absent while the pool was in use, so its DTL records the txgs it missed

model: Every device carries four labels, each with a copy of the pool configuration (a name-value list) and a ring of uberblocks. `zpool import` finds pools by reading only the configurations, in userspace, from every candidate device (or by reading the cachefile instead). The kernel never scans devices: it is handed a configuration and checks it.

Every import is done twice. First a tryimport opens the pool read-only under a temporary name to report its health, feature support and the host that uses it, then throws it away; `zpool import` with no pool name stops there. The real import starts again from that configuration.

The state that is loaded is the best uberblock found on any readable device: the highest txg (not above a requested maximum), then the latest timestamp. Its root block pointer opens the meta-object set (MOS), whose own copy of the configuration then replaces the one supplied by userspace. Nothing newer than that uberblock exists as far as the pool is concerned.

An import can be refused for several distinct reasons, checked in different places: zpool(8) itself refuses a pool that was not exported and was last used by another host, unless `-f`; with `multihost=on` the kernel watches the disks for another host's heartbeat and refuses whatever the flags say; unknown features refuse the import (only those needed for reading, with `-o readonly=on`); and missing devices refuse it when no redundancy covers them.

When the newest state cannot be loaded, `-F` walks back through older uberblocks still in the label rings, verifying each, and keeps the first that works, discarding the intent logs; `-X` allows going back further and verifies the whole pool; `-n` only reports what `-F` would do. Even without `-F` a failed import probes older txgs to tell you whether `-F` would help.

A writeable import changes the pool before you can use it: the uncommitted intent-log blocks are claimed so they are not reused, the sync thread starts, every label is rewritten with this host's id and the state ACTIVE, the cachefile is updated, and a resilver starts if any device missed writes. The logged writes themselves are replayed only when each file system is mounted. A read-only import skips all of this.

Export unmounts everything, waits until nothing holds the pool, then lets the last txgs sync with every label marked EXPORTED, closes the devices and removes the pool from the cachefile and from the kernel. A cleanly exported pool imports on any host without `-f`.
simplifications: Every `zpool import` runs the search and tryimport of path `discover` before the real import; the import paths show that part as a single step.

`spa_load()` is one node with many outgoing wires; the order of its phases is given in its role text and the paths, not by the layout. Phases with no effect on import decisions (checkpoint txg, indirect vdevs, removals, deferred destroys, initialize and TRIM restart) appear only in role text.

Label and uberblock reads go from the device straight to the code that uses them; the zio pipeline and the leaf driver in between (I/O flow graph) are not drawn. Likewise the MOS and verification reads are single wires to the data disks.
The cachefile and the label rings are shown as devices; the cachefile is really a file on the root file system.

Errors are drawn where they decide the outcome. Most also produce an ereport (`spa_load()`), a zfs_dbgmsg note and an import progress entry (`/proc/spl/kstat/zfs/import_progress`), which are left out.
zvol devices (created after import, removed at export, with their own ZIL replay), `-l` key loading, `-t`, `-V`, `-D` and the events sent to zed are left out.
The fallback of a failed cachefile import and the `-a` taskqs are shown once each; the repeated per-pool work is not drawn again.

page.title: ZFS Pool Import and Export
page.intro: This spec describes a diagram of how OpenZFS finds, imports and exports a pool: how `zpool import` discovers pools by reading the labels on candidate devices or the cachefile, how the kernel probes each candidate with a read-only tryimport, how the real import picks the uberblock (the pool state) to load, checks the devices, the host that last used the pool and the feature flags, rewinds to an older txg when asked, claims the intent logs and starts syncing, why an import is refused, what happens when the file systems are mounted afterwards, and what `zpool export` writes before the pool leaves the system.
